slides.text:
Until now a function was something you declared and called by name. In Go a function is also a **value**: you can keep it in a variable, hand it to another function, return it from one and put it in a list. You will do each of these.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
f = some function
f(3)

use(f)            pass it in
f = make_one()    get it back

slides.text: Write the name of a function **without parentheses** and you get the function itself, not its result. Store it in a variable, then call it through the variable with `()`.

A variable that holds a function has a **function type**: the word `func`, the types of the parameters and the type of the result. Two functions with the same parameters and result have the same type, so either one fits in the same variable.

These are types, not full code.
slides.code:
func(int) string
func(int, int) int
func(string) string

slides.text: A function can take another function as a parameter. Its type is written in the parameter list, and inside the function you call it like any other.

exercises.title: Store a function
exercises.guide: Put functions in variables, and call them from there.

chunks.text:
package main

import "fmt"

chunks.guide: The package and the import are already in the file. Two functions with the same shape.
A name with no parentheses is the function itself. The parentheses call it.

notes.text: Nothing runs yet: f just holds the function.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: `f` first holds `add1`, so `f(5)` is 6. The assignment `f = times2` puts a different function in the same variable, so the second `f(5)` is 10.

exercises.title: Spell the function type
exercises.guide: Declare a variable that holds a function, then switch which one.

chunks.text:
package main

import "fmt"

chunks.guide: The package and the import are already in the file. Two functions that take two ints and return one.
The variable has no value yet, only a type. Any function of that type can be assigned to it.

notes.text: Two ints in, one int out.

chunks.text:
func main() {
    var op func(int, int) int
    op = add
    fmt.Println(op(3, 4))
    op = multiply
    fmt.Println(op(3, 4))
}

exercises.title: Pass a function in
exercises.guide: Write a function that receives another function and uses it.

chunks.text:
package main

import "fmt"

chunks.guide: The package and the import are already in the file. Two functions to hand over later.
The second parameter has a function type. Inside, call it like any function.

notes.text: A parameter that holds a function.
Runs whichever function was passed in.

chunks.guide: Pass each function by its name, without parentheses.

exercises.title: Run it twice
exercises.guide: Fill the word that starts a function type, and the function to hand over.

slides.text: You can write a function with no name right where you need it: a **function literal**. Store it in a variable, or put `()` after it to run it at once.

A function can also **return** a function. Put a function type as the result type, and return a function value. The caller stores it and calls it.

The snippet is pseudo code.
Functions of the same type can live together in a slice. Walk the slice and call each one.

exercises.title: A function with no name
exercises.guide: Write a function right where you use it.

chunks.text:
package main

import "fmt"

chunks.guide: The package and the import are already in the file. A function with no name goes into a variable.

notes.text: A function written in place, with no name.

chunks.guide: Parentheses right after the literal run it on the spot.

notes.text: Defines the function and calls it right away.

exercises.title: Write it and run it
exercises.guide: Fill the word that starts a function with no name, and what runs the stored function.

exercises.title: Hand back a function
exercises.guide: Write a function that decides which function to return.

chunks.text:
package main

import "fmt"

chunks.guide: The package and the import are already in the file. Two functions to choose from.
The result type is a function type. Return a function by its name, with no parentheses.

notes.text: The result is itself a function.

chunks.guide: Store what comes back, then call it.

exercises.title: A list of functions
exercises.guide: Keep functions in a slice and call each one.

chunks.text:
package main

import "fmt"

chunks.guide: The package and the import are already in the file. Two functions of the same type.
The slice type says what its values are: functions from int to int. Call each one inside the loop.

notes.text: A list whose values are functions.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: `run(half, 9)` calls `half` with 9. Both are ints, so `9 / 2` is 4. Then `run(inc, a)` calls `inc` with 4 and gets 5.
